missing_or_wrong: Michelle's phone is canonically not damaged, but the scene repeatedly makes it cracked/broken/shattered and even 'damaged beyond repair'.
Turn 1 inspecting the phone should not invent damage and should provide useful consequence; instead it contradicts canon.
Turn 2 asks to search for Michelle's work bag and clues, but the narration mostly repeats entry material and phone damage, never actually resolving the requested search in a meaningful way.

The authored Scene 1A.1 evidence is not properly covered: missing tablet/work bag, overturned workstation chair, forced back door, and the newly carved KMS initials should accumulate into abduction suspicion. The scene barely uses these and never lands the suspicion.

Michelle's workstation drawers are canonically shut; turn 5/8 say Kristin starts searching through them, but no discovery or consequence follows, and the hidden-card setup is not meaningfully engaged.
The hidden memory card under the KMS-marked drawer is never found despite repeated apt searching of Michelle's workstation/work bag clues.
Kristin's laptop in her truck is never used, so Scene 1A.2 cannot occur.
The Continuity Initiative files, population stabilization centers, and Michelle's research note are never revealed, so Scene 1A.2 is skipped.
The interrupted voice recording and Michelle's warning 'Kristin, do not trust the emergency broadcasts.' are never revealed, so Scene 1A.3 is skipped.
The federal patrol beat is mishandled: there is only offscreen complication text, not a dramatized welfare check/search interaction with officers asking about Michelle's research.
The reflective tape marking on the front gate is never narrated, so Scene 1A.4 is skipped and no concrete return threat is established.
Beats are projected out of order and without payoff; from turn 2 onward the scene claims 1A.2/1A.3 while still failing to complete 1A.1.
Opening scene establishment is thin relative to the supplied opening requirement; it lacks substantial sensory grounding of the house as a crime scene.
Repeated turns recycle nearly identical responses without advancing the scene.
Cue text on turn 10 wrongly tags the KMS drawer clue to continuity_initiative_known and arrives extremely late after many failed searches.
No actionable lead to the park bench is ever given, so transition t_1a_1b is not earned.
reasons: Scene-local canon is violated by changing a protected setting fact: Michelle's phone is explicitly not damaged, yet the narration repeatedly describes it as cracked, shattered, broken, nonresponsive, and password-locked.
The scene does not stay local to the authored beat progression. It keeps reissuing entry-like descriptions and generic inspection text instead of moving through the specific 1A beats in order.

Progressive revelation fails because the scene stalls before the core discoveries. It neither converts the house evidence into serious abduction suspicion nor rewards workstation searching with the hidden card.
Investigation is not rewarded. The player repeatedly searches for the work bag, clues, and workstation, but receives loops and non-results instead of discoveries the canon says are here.

Scene 1A as authored requires all four sub-beats across the scene: gone/crime-scene evidence, memory card and files, interrupted message, then welfare-check threat. This scene skips 1A.2, 1A.3, and the dramatized content of 1A.4 entirely.

The patrol pressure appears only as meta complication text, not as narrated consequences the player actually experiences in-scene. The player never reads the officers' targeted questions or the gate marker.
Because no memory card, warning, or files are found, the player is never told what was found or where it points. Therefore no motivated exit or handoff to Scene 1B exists.

Protected knowledge is not leaked early, which is the one major area the scene preserves. But safety on protected knowledge is insufficient when the canonical facts and required scene beats are otherwise missed.
